Nema for Promotion readiness

Bring the promotion dependencies into one review.

Nema compares the campaign brief with stock, offer rules, assets, and owners. Commerce and marketing see unresolved dependencies before launch.

All use cases ↗

Gather the dependencies

Start with the approved promotion brief, offer rules, inventory snapshot, asset checklist, channel schedule, and owner list. Include effective dates, eligible products, exclusions, and the timestamp behind stock data.

Ask Nema to compare the records rather than assume that one system is current.

Prepare the readiness review

Nema can organize dependencies by ready, blocked, and needs confirmation. It can identify mismatched dates, missing owners, stock exceptions, and assets that lack approval.

The output is a review packet. It does not change prices, publish assets, or guarantee inventory.

Include cancellation and fallback criteria if the team has approved them. A promotion can be technically ready while a stock or legal dependency still makes launch unwise. Nema can display that condition without deciding whether to accept it.

Work across channels

Marketing and operations often own different parts of a promotion. Review the packet in the launch channel and tag the roles responsible for unresolved items. Nema can update the packet as owners confirm status.

A practical example

The landing page and paid campaign use the approved Friday start date, but the email shows Thursday. One promoted product is below the stock threshold in a stale warehouse snapshot. Nema flags both conflicts and asks the commerce owner to confirm the offer rules.

The owners update the date, refresh inventory, and approve the launch decision.

Keep decisions with owners

Commerce confirms price and offer logic. Inventory confirms stock interpretation. Marketing confirms assets and schedule. Nema brings their records together and prepares follow-ups without taking those decisions away from them.

After the decision, capture the approved dates, offer version, and owners in the thread. The final record should make clear which draft launched and which assumptions the team accepted.

Run a final check against the customer-facing assets, not only the internal checklist. The approved offer may be correct while one scheduled message still contains an earlier date or exclusion.

Record that check.

Common questions

Can Nema change promotion prices?

Not through this review. A price change needs a verified action and explicit authorization from the commerce owner.

Can Nema confirm stock availability?

It can show the current authorized snapshot and its timestamp. The inventory owner validates whether it is fit for the launch decision.

What if records disagree?

Keep the conflict visible, name the source and owner, and stop short of declaring the promotion ready.
